elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Section 3.4 as rendered: "Customer may terminate this Agreement (including all Service Option Attachments) or any Service Option Attachment ... for convenience at the end of any calendar month". The deterministic check "Customer convenience termination present: false" is a mechanical false negative (the operative words "Customer may terminate ... for convenience" are separated by the parenthetical carve-outs); in substance the right is present. The prerequisite-attachment carve-out narrows partial termination but does not remove the convenience right.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: "a. providing at least one month's prior written notice to IBM" — one month is not more than 30 days. Note (not a failure): the effective date is anchored to "the end of any calendar month", so the actual run-out can exceed 30 days; the notice requirement itself is compliant.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Neither the original nor the rendered Section 3.4 contains any refund obligation; the only payment mechanic runs the other way ("paying the applicable early termination charges"). No pro-rata prepaid-fee refund appears anywhere in the cited language, and the drafter expressly declined to pursue it. This is the element that keeps the preferred level incomplete.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: The cited provisions give IBM no mid-term no-cause exit: 3.2 is a non-renewal mechanic (notice "at least ninety (90) days prior to the end of the then-current term" preventing automatic renewal), which is evaluated under RENEWAL rather than as mid-term T4C, and the rationale identifies 3.3 as material-breach only. Nothing in the rendered text creates a Vendor convenience right.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: "at least one month's prior written notice to IBM" is shorter than the 60–90 day fallback window and therefore satisfies the Customer-protective requirement a fortiori (it also meets the 30-day preferred notice). The 60–90 day band is the relaxation of the preferred position, not a floor Customer must reach.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Operation 1 amends 3.4(b) to read "paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments, not to exceed three (3) months' charges." The cap is unconditional and sits on the only exit-fee mechanic; "charges" is the contract's own term for fees.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Condition satisfied on the record: IBM's sole no-cause exit is the 3.2 non-renewal election, whose effect is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term (notice "at least ninety (90) days prior to the end of the then-current term" defeating automatic renewal), and no other Vendor convenience right appears in the cited or rendered text.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Section 3.2 requires written notice "at least ninety (90) days prior to the end of the then-current term"; and because IBM has no separate convenience right, the element is in any event satisfied vacuously.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete after the edit: the Customer convenience right (one month's notice, better than 60–90 days) and the absence of any Vendor mid-term convenience right were already met, and the single gap — open-ended early termination charges cross-referenced to Attachment A and Service Option Attachments — is closed by the added cap "not to exceed three (3) months' charges."

Preferred is not complete solely because there is no pro-rata refund of prepaid fees on Customer's convenience termination; to reach preferred the drafter would need to insert an express obligation that IBM refund prepaid charges for the period after the effective date of termination, pro rata.

Minimal: the redline adds only the eight-word cap to Section 3.4(b), leaves the favourable one-month notice, the end-of-calendar-month mechanic, the prerequisite-attachment carve-out and the "if any" qualifier intact, and adds no survival, expense, refund or procedural extras outside the fallback checklist.

Preserves intent: the cap attaches to the existing charge mechanic without creating undefined terms or dangling cross-references; Attachment A and the Service Option Attachments continue to govern which charges apply, now subject to a ceiling. Minor drafting note (not a defect): "three (3) months' charges" does not state the measurement base, so consider "three (3) months' recurring charges for the terminated Service Option Attachment" if IBM pushes back on ambiguity.

Deterministic check "Customer convenience termination present = false" is inconsistent with the text and should be treated as a regex artefact; the operative sentence does grant Customer the convenience right, so it does not undermine the finding.

Classification as a deviation is supportable because an uncapped early-termination charge is a material failure of the fallback fee cap; the rationale correctly states the clause otherwise sits at (indeed above) the fallback and routes the 3.2 non-renewal mechanic to RENEWAL rather than double-flagging it here.
